taylor: quick heads-up — while onboarding mag-13b-int8-v2 I saw a consistent divergence for longcycle runs (>= 48k tokens). latency looks fine but outputs start drifting after the warmhead handoff.

raj: can you paste a short repro?

taylor: minimal repro is in the longbench suite. steps: run longbench/longcycle.sh with --quant int8 --sequence 50000.

- command:
```bash
./longbench/longcycle.sh --model mag-13b-int8-v2 --quant int8 --seq 50000 --runs 3
```

- observed: first ~30k tokens match fp16 baseline, after warmhead swap tokens diverge and KV indices look off in the logs.

anna: divergence as in semantics or token-by-token mismatch?

taylor: token-by-token mismatch. exact match until ~29872 then mismatch spikes. also saw increased kv-index-faults in runtime logs: sometimes writes at index > window_size.

sam: curious if it's timing-related (race on KV swap) or a RoPE scaling edge-case with quant rounding. any stack traces?

taylor: pasted trimmed logs below (sensitive values redacted):

```
[2026-03-21 14:02:31] prefill: tokens=29872, kv_write_idx=29872
[2026-03-21 14:02:31] warmhead-swap: swapping shards 3/8
[2026-03-21 14:02:31] post-swap-prefill: tokens=29873, kv_write_idx=32786  <-- unexpected jump
[2026-03-21 14:02:31] gen-step: rotary-index=29873, rot-scale=1.0
[2026-03-21 14:02:31] error: kv-index-out-of-range detected, clamped to window_end
```

raj: that kv_write_idx jump looks like a stride miscalc. Which runtime config? kernel-selection/dyn-batch?

taylor: default runtime config from canary: kernel_policy=auto, dynamic_batching=on, kv_mode=sharded-rotary, prefill_cache=true.

anna: try forcing kernel_policy=legacy and dynamic_batching=off for a quick A/B. I suspect the fused kernel path uses a different index packing for int8 prefill.

sam: I threw a quick run on canary-gpu-07 with kernel_policy=legacy, dynamic_batching=off. short 50k seq, int8. results: no index jumps in logs, outputs matched fp16 until end. latency went up ~12% though.

raj: can you drop numbers? throughput and p50 p99?

sam: from the quick run:
- fp16 baseline (canary-gpu-07): p50=42ms/token, p99=120ms/token, throughput=185 tokens/s
- int8 auto (broken path): p50=38ms/token, p99=110ms/token, throughput=205 tokens/s (but divergent)
- int8 legacy (safe): p50=44ms/token, p99=130ms/token, throughput=175 tokens/s

anna: so auto path is faster but corrupts KV indexes for longprefill. likely a packing/stride math difference introduced in int8 kernel refactor.

taylor: I added a failing unit test in runtime/tests/kv_index_stride_test.py that reproduces the jump deterministically (seeds included). filing a proper PR after we confirm root cause.

raj: nice. can ml-ci-bot run longbench with the new test and both kernel policies on canary? tagging @ml-ci-bot

ml-ci-bot: queued longbench job 1758880001 for canary-gpu-07. will post artifacts when done. :gear:

anna: quick mitigation for customers: add a guard in the prefill path that clamps kv_write_idx to prev_idx + seq_stride and log a throttled warning. avoid silent jumps.

taylor: agreed — I'll push a hotfix to add clamping + telemetry event kv.index_jump_detected (counts, model, seq_len, kernel_policy). also note it only hits on seq_len > 32k in our tests.

sam: FYI I ran a quick quantization compare on small set of eval prompts (50 long chats). int8-auto had ROUGE-L drop of ~4.8 points vs fp16 baseline after divergence, int8-legacy was within 0.6 points.

raj: ok let's do this plan:
1) roll clamping hotfix to canary (taylor)
2) run full longbench A/B across kernel_policy=auto/legacy + dynamic_batching on/off (ml-ci-bot)
3) if hotfix reduces incidents, prepare canary patch release and opt customers to legacy for long sequences until proper kernel fix
4) debug root cause in fused int8 prefill kernel (anna + sam)

taylor: assigning self for hotfix, pinging @anna and @sam for kernel debug. will open issue in repo with logs + failing test.

ml-ci-bot: longbench artifacts: job 1758880001 completed. summary uploaded: s3://redwood-longbench/1758880001/summary.json

raj: can someone grab the summary and paste the failure graphs?

sam: downloading now, will post highlights in the thread in a few mins. :mag_right:

anna: thanks all. keeping this high priority — long-context correctness is a blocker for the upcoming enterprise pilot.

taylor: opened issue #7123 with repro, logs, and test. PR for clamping ready and running unit tests. will request review.

raj: nice work. let's keep the canary pinned to legacy for customer tests until we have a green path. :thumbsup:
